_note: 12 reserved demo profiles for the customer app, one distinct customer each (cust_p01 .. cust_p12). Each profile has the data/demo-person.json shape, split per table: customer -> customers; home (null when the customer has no house) -> homes (customer_id = customer); objects -> insured_objects (object_id, class_id, name, history as JSON, details as JSON; profile as JSON for cottage/boat/car/dog, with a unique typeable key first: boat reg_no, car plate, dog chip_id, cottage property_id; the house is found by its address; the house keeps object_id = home_id and no profile column, its profile is in profiles instead); the house object's house_profile_values -> profiles.profile, expanded to the 20 fields of data/home-profile.schema.json the way backend/presets.py build does (value, confidence 0.9, source register, evidence {register: preset}, doubt false; every other field unknown); risks -> assigned_risks (texts from demo-person.json; risk_id is <template>@<object_id>, so engine.fix_value uses the rule default.<template>, which seed already creates); bids -> bids (customer_id = customer; firm names from fixtures/partners.json, each once per profile); tasks -> maintenance_tasks (customer_id = customer); reminders -> reminders (task ids). Scores: each insurance starts at 500 and adds its history points; the aggregate is the average; history sets score, band and tier. Premiums come from the class base premiums. Loader: the code of backend/db.py seed_presets, once per profile. profile_id, summary and classes are for people and checks; the loader ignores them.

risks.title: Ventilation filters not changed
risks.why: Clogged filters raise damp and energy use.
risks.explain: Ventilation filters need changing about once a year; clogged ones let damp build up.

risks.diy: Change the filters yourself, then book a duct check.

risks.title: Smoke alarms not tested
risks.why: A dead battery gives no warning in a fire.
risks.explain: Smoke alarms should be tested every few months and replaced after about ten years.

risks.diy: Press the test button on each alarm, then book a check if one fails.

risks.title: Electrical panel from 1994
risks.why: Old fuses can overheat and cause fires.
risks.explain: Your panel is original. Panels this old often lack residual-current protection, which is a common cause of house fires.
risks.fix: A certified electrician inspects the panel and adds a residual-current device if needed.
risks.diy: You cannot do electrical work yourself, but you can book an inspection to confirm the panel is safe.

risks.title: No water leak sensor
risks.why: A dishwasher leak can damage floors overnight.
risks.explain: Water damage is the most common home claim in Finland. A sensor with auto shut-off stops the water in seconds.
risks.fix: A partner installs leak sensors and a shut-off valve.
risks.diy: Place sensors under the dishwasher and sink yourself, then book a quick check.

risks.title: Thin attic insulation
risks.why: Heat loss can cause ice dams on the roof.
risks.explain: Insulation from 1994 is usually thinner than today's standard.
risks.fix: A partner measures and adds blown insulation.
risks.diy: Measure the insulation depth in the attic, then book a check.

risks.title: Pyry's vaccinations are out of date
risks.why: Parvovirus and distemper need long, costly care.
risks.explain: An unvaccinated dog can catch parvovirus or distemper, which need long and costly care.
risks.fix: A vet renews the vaccinations.
risks.diy: There is no way to do this yourself; book a vet visit.
